topic: Why 100 km on a map is not 100 km on the bike: how surface, heat, wind and rain change your riding day (and how to plan for it by splitting a route into 50 km segments)

content.hook: 100 km on the map. 9 hours on the bike.

scenes.text: POV: 100 km on the map... *9 hours* on the bike
Gravel, heat, headwind and rain all *slow you down*
Split the route into *50 km segments*. Plan each one.

content.caption:
Bikepacking route planning: 100 km on the map can mean a very long day on the bike. 🚲

Kilometres are only half the story.

Rough surface, heat, headwind and rain can each slow you down. Stack two or three and your "easy" day changes completely.

Fix: split the route into 50 km segments. Judge surface, heat, wind and rain for each one. Then plan your riding days from that, not from the total distance.

What slows you down most: surface, heat, wind or rain?

Free route plans with maps (Tour Divide, EuroVelo, Green Velo…): bikepackpilot.com/routes
